Then He said: ﴿For you therein is what your souls desire, and for you therein is what you ask for﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿what you ask for﴾ means what you wish for, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For them therein is fruit, and for them is what they ask for﴾ [Ya-Sin: 57]. If it is asked: according to this explanation, there is no difference between His saying ﴿For you therein is what your souls desire﴾ and His saying ﴿For you therein is what you ask for﴾. We answer: in my view, the closer interpretation is that His saying ﴿For you therein is what your souls desire﴾ refers to the bodily Paradise, and His saying ﴿For you therein is what you ask for﴾ refers to the spiritual Paradise mentioned in His saying: ﴿Their call therein is, "Glory be to You, O Allah," and their greeting therein is peace; and the last of their call is, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾ [Yunus: 10].

* * *

Then He said: ﴿As a welcome (nuzulan) from the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾. The nuzul is the provision of the guest (al-nazil), who is the visitor. Its placement is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal). The gnostics (al-'arifun) said: this verse indicates that all these mentioned things are in the manner of a nuzul. When the Generous gives the nuzul, He must then send precious robes of honour after it, and those precious robes are none other than the felicities attained at the vision, the manifestation, and the complete unveiling. We ask Allah, exalted is He, to make us worthy of them by His grace and generosity; indeed He is near, responsive.

Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast (الِاسْتِقامَة, istiqamah), the angels descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, and rejoice in the Paradise you were promised." We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. For you therein is what your souls desire, and for you therein is what you ask for. As a welcome from the Forgiving, the Merciful.

Know that when He, exalted is He, had dwelt at length on the threat, He followed it with this noble promise. This is a subtle arrangement on which the whole of the Qur'an revolves. We have mentioned repeatedly that perfections are of three kinds: the psychic (al-nafsaniyyah), the bodily (al-badaniyyah), and the external (al-kharijiyyah). The highest of these ranks is the psychic, the middle is the bodily, and the lowest is the external. We have also mentioned that psychic perfections are confined to two types: certain knowledge (al-'ilm al-yaqini) and righteous action (al-'amal al-salih). The people of verification (ahl al-tahqiq) said: the perfection of a human being lies in knowing the Truth for its own sake and the good for the sake of acting upon it. The head and chief of certain knowledge is the knowledge of Allah, and to this points His saying: ﴿Indeed those who say, "Our Lord is Allah"﴾. The head and chief of righteous deeds is that a person be upright in the middle, not inclining to either extreme of excess or deficiency, as He said: ﴿Thus We have made you a middle nation﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143], and He also said: ﴿Guide us to the straight path﴾. To this points His saying in this verse: ﴿then remained steadfast﴾.

I have heard that a reciter recited this verse in the assembly of al-'Abbadi, and al-'Abbadi said: "The resurrection is in the resurrection, according to the measure of steadfastness." Knowing this, we say: His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remained steadfast﴾ does not mean merely saying it with the tongue, because that alone does not produce steadfastness. Since steadfastness was mentioned after that saying, we know that the saying was accompanied by complete certainty and true knowledge. Knowing this, we say: concerning steadfastness there are two opinions:

The first: it means steadfastness in the religion, in monotheism (al-tawhid), and in knowledge.

The second: it means steadfastness in righteous deeds.

As for the first opinion, there are several expressions on it. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Then remained steadfast," i.e., they did not turn to any god other than Him. Ibn 'Abbas said in some narrations: this verse was revealed concerning Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, because Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, fell into severe kinds of affliction and trial, yet he never changed at all from his religion. He was the one who said: ﴿Our Lord is Allah﴾, and he remained steadfast upon it, not changing for any cause whatsoever.

I say: there are other aspects in this, namely that whoever affirms that this world has a God, there remain for him other stations. The first of them is that he should not go so far in affirmation as to end in anthropomorphism (al-tashbih), but should remain on the straight line dividing anthropomorphism from negation (al-ta'til). Likewise he must remain on the straight line dividing compulsion (al-jabr) from divine decree (al-qadar). Similarly, in hope and despair, he must remain on the straight line. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿Indeed those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," then remained steadfast﴾. As for the second opinion, which is that we understand steadfastness as the performing of righteous deeds, this is the view of a large group of the Companions and the Successors (al-tabi'un). They said: this is preferable, so that His saying ﴿Indeed those who say, "Our Lord is Allah"﴾ encompasses the saying and the belief, and His saying ﴿then remained steadfast﴾ encompasses the righteous deeds.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿the angels descend upon them﴾. It was said: at the time of death. It was also said: at three stations: at death, in the grave, and at the resurrection until the Final Day. ﴿Do not fear﴾: here "an" (أنْ) is in the sense of "ay" (أيْ, that is), or it is the lightened form (مُخَفَّفَة) of the heavy "anna" (أنَّ), and its original is "bi-annahu la takhafu," where the "ha'" is the pronoun of the matter (ضَمِيرُ الشَّأْنِ). Know that the ultimate aim in safeguarding interests is the repelling of harms and the securing of benefits. It is well known that repelling harm takes precedence over securing benefit. Harm either occurs in the future, or in the present, or in the past. Here there is a subtle rational point: the future precedes the present, and the present precedes the past. For a thing that has not yet existed and whose occurrence is anticipated is future; when it exists it becomes present; when it perishes and passes away after that, it becomes past. Also, the future draws nearer to attainment every hour, while the past becomes further from attainment in every state. For this reason the poet said:

"May what you desire never cease to be nearer than tomorrow,
and may what you fear never cease to be further than yesterday."

Since this is established, harms anticipated to occur in the future deserve repelling more than past harms. Also, fear (al-khawf) is the pain of the heart caused by the anticipation of harm in the future, and grief (al-hazn) is the pain of the heart caused by the loss of a benefit that existed in the past. Given this, repelling fear takes precedence over repelling the grief that arises from sorrow. Knowing this, we say: He, exalted is He, informed about the angels that at the outset they announce that there is no fear upon you concerning what you will encounter of the states of the Resurrection. Then they announce that there is no grief upon you concerning what has escaped you of the affairs of the world. When these two matters are attained, harms and hardships have wholly vanished.

Then, after this is complete, they give them the good news (yubashsharun) of the attainment of benefits, and this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and rejoice in the Paradise you were promised﴾. If it is asked: glad tidings (al-bisharah) is the first report of the attainment of a benefit. When a man reports to someone that a benefit has been attained, and then reports a second time that it has been attained, the second report is an informing and not glad tidings. The believer often hears good tidings of goodness, so when the believer hears this report from the angels, it should be an informing and not glad tidings. What is the reason for calling this report glad tidings? We answer: the believer hears that whoever is a believing and pious person has Paradise. As for one who has never heard at all that he is among the people of Paradise, when he hears this speech from the angels, it is an informing of a great benefit, and since it is the first report of that, it is glad tidings.

Know that this speech indicates that the believer, at death, in the grave, and at the resurrection, is not panicked by the terrors and by severe dread, but is secure of heart and tranquil of breast. For His saying ﴿Do not fear and do not grieve﴾ conveys the negation of fear and grief in an absolute sense.

Then He, exalted is He, informed about the angels that they said to the believers: ﴿We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾. This stands in contrast to what He mentioned in the threat against the disbelievers, when He said: ﴿And We appointed for them companions﴾ [Fussilat: 25]. The meaning of their being allies to the believers is that the angels have influences upon human spirits through inspirations and certain unveilings (al-mukashafat), and through true stations, just as the devils have influences upon spirits by casting whisperings into them and presenting falsehoods to them.

In sum, the angels being allies to pure and purified spirits arises from many aspects that are known to the people of unveilings and direct witnessing. They say: just as that allegiance existed in the world, it will remain in the Hereafter, for those bonds are intrinsic, necessary, and not subject to cessation. Rather, after death they become even stronger and more lasting. This is because the essence of the soul is of the kind of the angels. It is like a spark in relation to fire, or a drop in relation to the sea. The bodily attachments are what intervene between it and the angels, as he, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Were it not that the devils hover over the hearts of the children of Adam, they would look upon the dominion of the heavens." When the bodily attachments and bodily management are removed, the covering and the obstruction are gone, so the effect joins the influencer, the drop joins the sea, and the spark joins the sun. This is what is meant by His saying: ﴿We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾.

Ibn 'Abbas said: ﴿what you ask for﴾ means what you wish for, like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿For them therein is fruit, and for them is what they ask for﴾ [Ya-Sin: 57]. Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 41, verses 33–36 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah and does righteousness and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"?﴾ ﴿Good and evil are not equal. Repel [evil] by that which is better; and thereupon the one between whom and you there is enmity will be as though he were a devoted friend.﴾ ﴿But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune.﴾ ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should tempt you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.﴾

Know that in this verse there are several issues:

The first issue: We have mentioned that the discourse from the beginning of this surah was initiated where they said to the Messenger, ﴿Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you invite us﴾ [Fussilat: 5], and their intention was that they would not accept your speech nor pay attention to your proof. Then they mentioned another way of folly, saying, ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk noisily during it﴾ [Fussilat: 26]. Allah, glorified is He, mentioned the sufficient answers and the adequate clear proofs in repelling these doubts and removing these misguidances. Then Allah, glorified and exalted is He, explained that even though these people uttered these corrupt words, it is obligatory upon you to continuously persevere in conveying and calling to the truth, for calling to the true religion is the most complete of acts of obedience and the foremost of acts of worship. He expressed this meaning by saying: ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah and does righteousness and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"?﴾ This is a noble and good aspect in the arrangement of the verses of this surah. There is another aspect in it, which is that the levels of felicity are two: the complete, and what is above the complete. As for the complete, it is that one acquires from the virtuous attributes that by which he becomes perfect in his own self. When he finishes from this rank, he then occupies himself with perfecting those who are deficient, and this is above the complete. Knowing this, we say: His saying, ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah" and then remain steadfast﴾ [Fussilat: 30], is an indication of the first rank, which is acquiring the states that bring about the perfection of the soul in its essence. When one is free from this rank, it becomes obligatory to move to the second rank, which is occupying oneself with perfecting the deficient, and that is only through calling the creation to the true religion, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah﴾. This too is a good aspect in the arrangement of these verses.

Know that whoever Allah has granted a strong natural disposition and a sufficient share of divine, unveiling knowledge, will know that there is no arrangement better or more complete than the arrangement of the verses of the Qur'an.

The second issue: Some people said that what is meant by His saying, ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah﴾, is the Messenger ﷺ, and among them are those who said: they are the muezzins. But the definitively established truth is that everyone who calls to Allah by any of the means is included in it. And calling to Allah has ranks:

The first rank: the call of the Prophets, peace be upon them, is superior to the call of others in several respects:

The first of them: they combined calling with proof first, then calling with the sword second, and it has rarely happened to others to combine these two methods.

The second of them: they were the initiators of this call, whereas the scholars build their call upon the call of the Prophets, and initiating a noble matter in the way of beginning is more excellent.

The third of them: their souls were stronger in power and their spirits purer in substance, so their influence in reviving dead hearts and illuminating murky spirits was more complete, and thus their call was more excellent.

The fourth of them: souls are of three kinds: deficient; complete but unable to perfect the deficient; and complete and able to perfect the deficient.

The first kind is the common people; the second kind are the saints (awliya'); and the third kind are the prophets. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ said: "The scholars of my community are like the prophets of the Children of Israel." Knowing this, we say: the soul of the prophets has two distinctions: perfection in essence and perfecting others. Thus their strength in calling was greater, and their ranks were more excellent and more complete.

Knowing this, we say: the prophets, peace be upon them, have two attributes: knowledge and power. As for the scholars, they are the deputies of the prophets in knowledge; and as for the kings, they are the deputies of the prophets in power. Knowledge necessitates dominion over spirits, and power necessitates dominion over bodies. So the scholars are the successors of the prophets in the world of spirits, and the kings are the successors of the prophets in the world of bodies.

Knowing this, it becomes clear that the most complete rank in calling to Allah after the prophets is the rank of the scholars. Then the scholars are of three kinds: scholars of Allah, scholars of the attributes of Allah, and scholars of the rulings of Allah.

As for the scholars of Allah, they are the wise (hukama') about whom Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿He gives wisdom to whom He wills, and whoever has been given wisdom has certainly been given much good﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 269]. As for the scholars of the attributes of Allah, exalted is He, they are the people of the principles (usul). As for the scholars of the rulings of Allah, they are the jurists (fuqaha'). Each of these stations has three ranks without end, so for this reason calling to Allah has ranks without end.

As for the kings, they too call to the religion of Allah by the sword, and that is in two ways: either by establishing it when it is absent, such as fighting against the disbelievers, or by enforcing it when it is present, such as our saying: the apostate is to be killed.

As for the muezzins, they enter this category only weakly. Their entry into it is because the recitation of the words of the adhan is a call to prayer, so that falls under calling to Allah. As for this rank being weak, it is because the apparent state of the muezzin is that he does not comprehend the meanings of those words, and even if he were to comprehend them, he does not intend by their recitation those noble meanings. This is the discussion concerning the ranks of calling to Allah.

The third issue: His saying, ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah﴾, indicates that calling to Allah is better than everything else. Knowing this, we say: every act that is the best of deeds must be obligatory, because whatever is not obligatory, the obligatory is better than it. Knowing this, we say: calling to Allah is the best of deeds by the requirement of this verse, and whatever is the best of deeds is obligatory. Therefore it follows that calling to Allah is obligatory. Then we say: the adhan is a call to Allah, and calling to Him is obligatory, so it follows: the adhan is obligatory. Know that most of the jurists claimed that the adhan is not obligatory, and they claimed that the adhan is not included in this verse. The decisive proof against this is that the call intended in this verse must be the best of speech. And it is established that the adhan is not the best of speech, because calling to the religion of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, by certain proofs is better than the adhan. It follows by the second figure that what is included under this verse is not the adhan.

The fourth issue: People have differed as to whether it is preferable for a man to say, "I am a Muslim," or whether it is preferable to say, "I am a Muslim, if Allah wills." Those who hold the first view argued for the soundness of their position by this verse, for the implication is: "And who is better in speech than one who says, 'Indeed, I am of the Muslims'?" So He judged that this statement is the best of statements. And if our saying, "if Allah wills," were considered in making it the best of statements, the implication of the apparent meaning of this verse would be invalidated.

The fifth issue: The verse indicates that the best of speech is the speech of one who combines three qualities. The first of them: calling to Allah. The second: righteous deeds. The third: that he be among the Muslims. As for calling to Allah, we have explained it, and it is an expression for calling to Allah by establishing certain proofs and definitive demonstrations.

* * *

As for His saying, ﴿and does righteousness﴾, know that righteous deeds are either deeds of the heart, which is knowledge (ma'rifah), or deeds of the limbs, which are all the acts of obedience.

* * *

As for His saying, ﴿and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"﴾, it is that there is joined to the deed of the heart and the deed of the limbs the affirmation by the tongue. Thus this man is described by four qualities: the first of them: affirmation by the tongue; the second: righteous deeds by the limbs; the third: correct belief in the heart; the fourth: occupying oneself with establishing the proof for the religion of Allah. There is no doubt that the one described by these four qualities is the noblest and most excellent of people, and the perfection of rank in these four stations belongs only to Muhammad ﷺ.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Good and evil are not equal.﴾ Know that we have made clear that the discourse from the beginning of the surah started from Allah relating of them that they said: ﴿Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you invite us﴾ [Fussilat: 5]. They thus displayed from themselves a severe persistence in their former religions and a lack of being affected by the proofs of Muhammad ﷺ. Then He, exalted is He, elaborated greatly in answering this, mentioning many aspects, and followed them with promise and warning. Then He related another doubt from them, which is their saying: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk noisily during it﴾ [Fussilat: 26], and He answered this also with many aspects. Then He, exalted is He, after the elaborate answer to those doubts, encouraged Muhammad ﷺ not to abandon calling to Allah.

He began first by saying: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah" and then remain steadfast﴾, so for them is the great reward. Then He ascended from that rank to another rank, which is that calling to Allah is among the greatest ranks. Thus the discourse from the beginning of the surah up to this point came in the best arrangement. Then it is as though a questioner asked, saying: calling to Allah, although it is a great act of obedience, yet patience over the folly of these disbelievers is severe, and we have no capacity for it. At this point Allah mentioned what is suitable to be a remover of this difficulty, saying: ﴿Good and evil are not equal.﴾ By "the good" is meant the call of the Messenger ﷺ to the true religion, patience over the ignorance of the disbelievers, abandoning retaliation, and not turning to them. By "the evil" is meant the coarseness they displayed in their saying: ﴿Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you invite us﴾, and what they mentioned in their saying: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk noisily during it﴾. So it is as though He said: O Muhammad, your action is good and their action is evil, and good and evil are not equal, meaning that when you perform this good, you deserve honor in this world and reward in the Hereafter, whereas they are the opposite of that. Therefore their persistence in that evil should not prevent you from occupying yourself with this good.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿Repel [evil] by that which is better﴾, meaning: repel their folly and ignorance by the way that is the best of ways. For when you are patient over their bad character time after time, and do not meet their folly with anger, nor their harm with injury and alienation, they will become ashamed of those blameworthy characters and abandon those ugly actions.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿and thereupon the one between whom and you there is enmity will be as though he were a devoted friend.﴾ Meaning: when you meet their evil with good and their ugly actions with good actions, they will abandon their ugly actions and turn from enmity to love, and from hatred to affection. When Allah, exalted is He, guided to this path, which is beneficial in religion, in this world, and in the Hereafter, He magnified it, saying: ﴿But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune.﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: That is, none is granted this act except those who are patient in bearing hardships, enduring adversities, swallowing anger, and abandoning retaliation.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And none is granted it except those who are endowed with a great portion﴾ of the soul's excellences and a lofty rank in spiritual strength. For engaging in retaliation and repulsion arises only after the soul has been affected, and the soul's being affected by external incursions arises only when the soul is weak. As for when the soul is strong in its essence, it is not affected by external incursions; and when it is not affected by them, it does not weaken, is not harmed, and does not engage in retaliation. Thus it is established that this conduct which we have explained is granted only to one who possesses a great portion of the strength of soul, purity of essence, and cleanliness of self.

It is also possible that the meaning is: ﴿And none is granted it except one who has a great portion﴾ of the reward of the Hereafter. In this case, His saying ﴿And none is granted it except those who are patient﴾ is praise for the act of patience, and His saying ﴿And none is granted it except one who has a great portion﴾ is a promise of the greatest portion of reward.

Having mentioned this complete method of repelling anger and retaliation, and of abandoning enmity, He mentioned after it another method, also greatly beneficial in this regard, saying: ﴿And if an incitement from Satan incites you, then seek refuge in Allah; indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾. This verse, together with the great benefits it contains, is explained thoroughly at the end of Surat al-A'raf. The author of al-Kashshaf said: "Nazgh (incitement) and nasgh have the same meaning, and it is like a prod (nakhs). Satan incites a person, as if he prods him by urging him toward what is not fitting. Nazgh was made into the agent (nazigh), as is said: 'Jaddu jiddihi' (his effort is serious). Or the intended meaning of ﴿And if an incitement [nazghun] from Satan incites you﴾ is that 'nazigh' is a descriptive of Satan, using the verbal noun."

In sum, the purpose of the verse is: even if Satan diverts you from what I have prescribed of repelling evil with what is better, then seek refuge in Allah from his evil, proceed on your course, and do not obey him. And Allah knows best.

Therefore it follows that calling to Allah is obligatory. Then we say: the adhan is a call to Allah, and calling to Him is obligatory, so it follows: the adhan is obligatory. Know that most of the jurists claimed that the adhan is not obligatory, and they claimed that the adhan is not included in this verse. The decisive proof against this is that the call intended in this verse must be the best of speech. And it is established that the adhan is not the best of speech, because calling to the religion of Allah, glorified and exalted is He, by certain proofs is better than the adhan. It follows by the second figure that what is included under this verse is not the adhan.

The fourth issue: People have differed as to whether it is preferable for a man to say, "I am a Muslim," or whether it is preferable to say, "I am a Muslim, if Allah wills." Those who hold the first view argued for the soundness of their position by this verse, for the implication is: "And who is better in speech than one who says, 'Indeed, I am of the Muslims'?" So He judged that this statement is the best of statements. And if our saying, "if Allah wills," were considered in making it the best of statements, the implication of the apparent meaning of this verse would be invalidated.

The fifth issue: The verse indicates that the best of speech is the speech of one who combines three qualities. The first of them: calling to Allah. The second: righteous deeds. The third: that he be among the Muslims. As for calling to Allah, we have explained it, and it is an expression for calling to Allah by establishing certain proofs and definitive demonstrations.

* * *

As for His saying, ﴿and does righteousness﴾, know that righteous deeds are either deeds of the heart, which is knowledge (ma'rifah), or deeds of the limbs, which are all the acts of obedience.

* * *

As for His saying, ﴿and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"﴾, it is that there is joined to the deed of the heart and the deed of the limbs the affirmation by the tongue. Thus this man is described by four qualities: the first of them: affirmation by the tongue; the second: righteous deeds by the limbs; the third: correct belief in the heart; the fourth: occupying oneself with establishing the proof for the religion of Allah. There is no doubt that the one described by these four qualities is the noblest and most excellent of people, and the perfection of rank in these four stations belongs only to Muhammad ﷺ.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Good and evil are not equal.﴾ Know that we have made clear that the discourse from the beginning of the surah started from Allah relating of them that they said: ﴿Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you invite us﴾ [Fussilat: 5]. They thus displayed from themselves a severe persistence in their former religions and a lack of being affected by the proofs of Muhammad ﷺ. Then He, exalted is He, elaborated greatly in answering this, mentioning many aspects, and followed them with promise and warning. Then He related another doubt from them, which is their saying: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk noisily during it﴾ [Fussilat: 26], and He answered this also with many aspects. Then He, exalted is He, after the elaborate answer to those doubts, encouraged Muhammad ﷺ not to abandon calling to Allah.

He began first by saying: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah" and then remain steadfast﴾, so for them is the great reward. Then He ascended from that rank to another rank, which is that calling to Allah is among the greatest ranks. Thus the discourse from the beginning of the surah up to this point came in the best arrangement. Then it is as though a questioner asked, saying: calling to Allah, although it is a great act of obedience, yet patience over the folly of these disbelievers is severe, and we have no capacity for it. At this point Allah mentioned what is suitable to be a remover of this difficulty, saying: ﴿Good and evil are not equal.﴾ By "the good" is meant the call of the Messenger ﷺ to the true religion, patience over the ignorance of the disbelievers, abandoning retaliation, and not turning to them. By "the evil" is meant the coarseness they displayed in their saying: ﴿Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you invite us﴾, and what they mentioned in their saying: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk noisily during it﴾. So it is as though He said: O Muhammad, your action is good and their action is evil, and good and evil are not equal, meaning that when you perform this good, you deserve honor in this world and reward in the Hereafter, whereas they are the opposite of that. Therefore their persistence in that evil should not prevent you from occupying yourself with this good.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿Repel [evil] by that which is better﴾, meaning: repel their folly and ignorance by the way that is the best of ways. For when you are patient over their bad character time after time, and do not meet their folly with anger, nor their harm with injury and alienation, they will become ashamed of those blameworthy characters and abandon those ugly actions.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿and thereupon the one between whom and you there is enmity will be as though he were a devoted friend.﴾ Meaning: when you meet their evil with good and their ugly actions with good actions, they will abandon their ugly actions and turn from enmity to love, and from hatred to affection. When Allah, exalted is He, guided to this path, which is beneficial in religion, in this world, and in the Hereafter, He magnified it, saying: ﴿But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune.﴾ Al-Zajjaj said: That is, none is granted this act except those who are patient in bearing hardships, enduring adversities, swallowing anger, and abandoning retaliation.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And none is granted it except those who are endowed with a great portion﴾ of the soul's excellences and a lofty rank in spiritual strength. For engaging in retaliation and repulsion arises only after the soul has been affected, and the soul's being affected by external incursions arises only when the soul is weak. As for when the soul is strong in its essence, it is not affected by external incursions; and when it is not affected by them, it does not weaken, is not harmed, and does not engage in retaliation. Thus it is established that this conduct which we have explained is granted only to one who possesses a great portion of the strength of soul, purity of essence, and cleanliness of self.

It is also possible that the meaning is: ﴿And none is granted it except one who has a great portion﴾ of the reward of the Hereafter. In this case, His saying ﴿And none is granted it except those who are patient﴾ is praise for the act of patience, and His saying ﴿And none is granted it except one who has a great portion﴾ is a promise of the greatest portion of reward.

Having mentioned this complete method of repelling anger and retaliation, and of abandoning enmity, He mentioned after it another method, also greatly beneficial in this regard, saying: ﴿And if an incitement from Satan incites you, then seek refuge in Allah; indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾. This verse, together with the great benefits it contains, is explained thoroughly at the end of Surat al-A'raf. The author of al-Kashshaf said: "Nazgh (incitement) and nasgh have the same meaning, and it is like a prod (nakhs). Satan incites a person, as if he prods him by urging him toward what is not fitting. Nazgh was made into the agent (nazigh), as is said: 'Jaddu jiddihi' (his effort is serious). Or the intended meaning of ﴿And if an incitement [nazghun] from Satan incites you﴾ is that 'nazigh' is a descriptive of Satan, using the verbal noun."

In sum, the purpose of the verse is: even if Satan diverts you from what I have prescribed of repelling evil with what is better, then seek refuge in Allah from his evil, proceed on your course, and do not obey him. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 41, verses 37–39:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah who created them, if it is Him you worship.﴾ ﴿But if they are arrogant, those who are with your Lord glorify Him night and day, and they never tire.﴾ ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth humbled, but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells. Indeed, He who revives it is surely the Reviver of the dead. Indeed, He is over all things Competent.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, had explained in the preceding verse that the best of deeds and words is the call to Allah, exalted is He, He followed it with mention of the proofs that indicate the existence of Allah, His power and His wisdom, as an alert that the call to Allah, exalted is He, is an expression of establishing the proofs that indicate the essence of Allah and His attributes. These are noble admonitions derived from the coherence of these verses, and knowledge of these subtleties is among the best sciences of the Qur'an. You have also learned that the proofs indicating these lofty matters are the knowledge of everything in it of parts and components. So He begins here with mention of the celestial things, which are the night and the day.

The mention of the night was placed before the mention of the day as an alert that darkness is non-existence and light is existence, and non-existence precedes existence. This is like an alert to the origination (huduth) of these things. As for the indication of the sun, the moon, the spheres and the rest of the stars upon the existence of the Creator (al-Sani'), we have explained it in this book many times, especially in the commentary on His saying: ﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Fatiha: 2], and in the commentary on His saying: ﴿Praise be to Allah who created the heavens and the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 1].

When He explained that the sun and the moon are originated, and that they are two proofs of the existence of the capable God, He said: ﴿Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon﴾, meaning that they are two servants, two proofs of the existence of God. Prostration (sujud) is an expression of the utmost veneration, so it is not fitting except for one who is the most noble of existing things. So He said: ﴿Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon﴾, because they are two created servants, ﴿but prostrate to Allah﴾, the Creator, the Capable, the Wise. The pronoun in His saying ﴿who created them﴾ refers to the night, the day and the moon, because the ruling for a group of non-rational things is the ruling for the feminine singular or feminine plural. It is said of pens: "I sharpened them" (bariytuha) and "I sharpened them" (bariytuhunna). And when He said ﴿among His signs﴾, they were in the sense of feminine plurals, so He said ﴿who created them﴾. And He said ﴿if it is Him you worship﴾ because some people used to prostrate to the sun and the moon, like the Sabians in their worship of the stars, and they claimed that by prostrating to them they intended prostration to Allah. So they were forbidden from this intermediary and commanded that they should prostrate only to Allah who created things. If it is said: if there must be a specific qibla in prayer, then if we made the sun a specific qibla at the time of prostration, that would be better. We say: the sun is a shining substance of great elevation and high rank, so if the Law permitted making it a qibla in prayers, then with habituation to prostrating toward the side of the sun, it might well prevail upon people's imaginations that this prostration is to the sun and not to Allah.

Page 112

Therefore, out of fear of this prohibited outcome, the Wise Lawgiver forbade making the sun a qibla for prostration, unlike a specific stone, for there is nothing in it that suggests divinity. So the purpose of the qibla was attained and the mentioned danger was removed, and this is better. Know that the school of al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, is that the place of prostration (of recitation) is His saying ﴿you worship﴾, because His saying ﴿and prostrate to Allah﴾ is connected to it. According to Abu Hanifa, it is His saying ﴿and they never tire﴾, because the statement is complete in his view.

Then, when He, exalted is He, commanded prostration, He said after it: ﴿But if they are arrogant, those who are with your Lord glorify Him night and day, and they never tire.﴾ And concerning this there are questions:

The first question: Those who prostrate to the sun and the moon say: "We are too lowly and too humble to attain the capacity of worshipping Allah, exalted is He, but we are slaves to the sun, and they are two servants of Allah." If this is their statement, how is it fitting to say that they were arrogant toward prostrating to Allah?

The answer: The meaning of the word "arrogance" is not what you mention. Rather, the meaning is: if they are arrogant toward accepting your word, O Muhammad, in the prohibition against prostrating to the sun and the moon.

The second question: The Mushabbiha (anthropomorphists) held onto His saying ﴿those who are with your Lord﴾ to establish place and direction for Allah, exalted is He. The answer: It is said: "with the king are such-and-such soldiers," and by it is not meant nearness of place. So likewise here. This is indicated by His saying: "I am with my servant's opinion of me, and I am with those whose hearts are broken for My sake" ("in a seat of truth with a Mighty King"). And it is said, according to al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, that a Muslim is not killed for a dhimmi.

The third question: Does this verse indicate that the angel is more excellent than man? The answer: Yes, because one reasons from the state of the higher to the state of the lower. It is said: these peoples, if they are arrogant toward obeying so-and-so, then the great ones serve him and acknowledge his precedence. Thus it is established that this kind of reasoning is only fitting from the state of the higher to the state of the lower.

The fourth question: Here He said concerning the angels: ﴿They glorify night and day﴾, and this indicates that they are constant in glorification, never separated from it for a single moment, and their occupation with this work on a continuous basis prevents them from occupation with other works, such as descending to the earth, as He said: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 193], and He said: ﴿And inform them of the guests of Ibrahim﴾ [al-Hijr: 51], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Over it are angels, stern and severe﴾ [al-Tahrim: 6].

The answer: Those whom Allah, exalted is He, mentioned here as constant in glorification are specific groups of angels, namely the noblest and greatest of them, because He described them as being with Him, and what is meant by this "withness" is the perfection of nobility and honor. This does not contradict that another group of angels is occupied with other works. If they say: suppose the matter is as such, but they must breathe, and their occupation with that breathing diverts them from that state of glorification. We say: just as breathing is a cause for the well-being of life for humans, so the remembrance of Allah, exalted is He, is a cause for the well-being of their state in their life. And it is not required of a rational, fair person to measure the states of the angels, in the purity of their substance, the radiance of their essences and their absorption in the ascending paths of the knowledge of Allah, by the states of humans, for indeed between the two states is the distance of the two easts.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth humbled.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, mentioned the four celestial signs, which are the night, the day, the sun and the moon, He followed them with mention of an earthly sign

Page 113

so He said: ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth humbled.﴾ Khushu' is submission and abasement, and this word is borrowed for the state of the earth when it is empty of rain and vegetation. ﴿But when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells.﴾ That is, it moves with plants. Rabat means it swells, because when a plant is about to emerge the earth rises and swells for it, then it splits open with the plant. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, He who revives it is surely the Reviver of the dead.﴾ That is, the One capable of reviving the earth after its death is the One capable of reviving these bodies after their death. We have mentioned the explanation of this proof many times, in countless places. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, He is over all things Competent.﴾ This is the original proof, and its explanation: the return of composition and assembly to those scattered parts is possible in its essence, and the return of life, intellect and power to those parts after their gathering is also possible in its essence, and Allah, exalted is He, is capable of possibilities, so it must be that He is capable of restoring composition, assembly, life, power, intellect and understanding to those parts. This clearly indicates that the resurrection of bodies is possible, with no impossibility in it whatsoever. And Allah knows best.

Then, when He, exalted is He, commanded prostration, He said after it: ﴿But if they are arrogant, those who are with your Lord glorify Him night and day, and they never tire.﴾ And concerning this there are questions:

The first question: Those who prostrate to the sun and the moon say: "We are too lowly and too humble to attain the capacity of worshipping Allah, exalted is He, but we are slaves to the sun, and they are two servants of Allah." If this is their statement, how is it fitting to say that they were arrogant toward prostrating to Allah?

The answer: The meaning of the word "arrogance" is not what you mention. Rather, the meaning is: if they are arrogant toward accepting your word, O Muhammad, in the prohibition against prostrating to the sun and the moon.

The second question: The Mushabbiha (anthropomorphists) held onto His saying ﴿those who are with your Lord﴾ to establish place and direction for Allah, exalted is He. The answer: It is said: "with the king are such-and-such soldiers," and by it is not meant nearness of place. So likewise here. This is indicated by His saying: "I am with my servant's opinion of me, and I am with those whose hearts are broken for My sake" ("in a seat of truth with a Mighty King"). And it is said, according to al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, that a Muslim is not killed for a dhimmi.

The third question: Does this verse indicate that the angel is more excellent than man? The answer: Yes, because one reasons from the state of the higher to the state of the lower. It is said: these peoples, if they are arrogant toward obeying so-and-so, then the great ones serve him and acknowledge his precedence. Thus it is established that this kind of reasoning is only fitting from the state of the higher to the state of the lower.

The fourth question: Here He said concerning the angels: ﴿They glorify night and day﴾, and this indicates that they are constant in glorification, never separated from it for a single moment, and their occupation with this work on a continuous basis prevents them from occupation with other works, such as descending to the earth, as He said: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down upon your heart﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 193], and He said: ﴿And inform them of the guests of Ibrahim﴾ [al-Hijr: 51], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Over it are angels, stern and severe﴾ [al-Tahrim: 6].

The answer: Those whom Allah, exalted is He, mentioned here as constant in glorification are specific groups of angels, namely the noblest and greatest of them, because He described them as being with Him, and what is meant by this "withness" is the perfection of nobility and honor. This does not contradict that another group of angels is occupied with other works. If they say: suppose the matter is as such, but they must breathe, and their occupation with that breathing diverts them from that state of glorification. We say: just as breathing is a cause for the well-being of life for humans, so the remembrance of Allah, exalted is He, is a cause for the well-being of their state in their life. And it is not required of a rational, fair person to measure the states of the angels, in the purity of their substance, the radiance of their essences and their absorption in the ascending paths of the knowledge of Allah, by the states of humans, for indeed between the two states is the distance of the two easts.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth humbled.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, mentioned the four celestial signs, which are the night, the day, the sun and the moon, He followed them with mention of an earthly sign

Page 113

so He said: ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth humbled.﴾ Khushu' is submission and abasement, and this word is borrowed for the state of the earth when it is empty of rain and vegetation. ﴿But when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells.﴾ That is, it moves with plants. Rabat means it swells, because when a plant is about to emerge the earth rises and swells for it, then it splits open with the plant. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, He who revives it is surely the Reviver of the dead.﴾ That is, the One capable of reviving the earth after its death is the One capable of reviving these bodies after their death. We have mentioned the explanation of this proof many times, in countless places. Then He said: ﴿Indeed, He is over all things Competent.﴾ This is the original proof, and its explanation: the return of composition and assembly to those scattered parts is possible in its essence, and the return of life, intellect and power to those parts after their gathering is also possible in its essence, and Allah, exalted is He, is capable of possibilities, so it must be that He is capable of restoring composition, assembly, life, power, intellect and understanding to those parts. This clearly indicates that the resurrection of bodies is possible, with no impossibility in it whatsoever. And Allah knows best.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 41, verses 40–42:**

The Most High said: ﴿Indeed, those who distort Our signs are not hidden from Us. Is one who is thrown into the Fire better, or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection? Do as you wish; indeed He is Seeing of what you do.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it comes to them [will be punished]. And indeed it is a Book of might.﴾ ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it; it is a revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy.﴾

Know that when the Most High explained that calling to the religion of God is the greatest of positions and the most noble of ranks, and then explained that calling to the religion of God is only achieved by mentioning the proofs of monotheism (tawhid), justice, the validity of resurrection and the Last Day, He returned to threatening those who dispute these signs and try to cast doubts upon them. So He said: ﴿Indeed, those who distort Our signs﴾. It is said: ﴿ألْحَدَ﴾ (alhada) and ﴿لَحَدَ﴾ (lahada) when the digger (al-hafir) deviates from straightness and digs in a side (shiqq). Thus the ﴿مُلْحِد﴾ (mulhid, one who distorts) is the one who deviates. Then, by customary usage, the word became specific to one who deviates from the truth towards falsehood.

His saying ﴿are not hidden from Us﴾ is a threat, like when a formidable king says: "Indeed, those who dispute my kingship, I know them," which is a threat. Then He said: ﴿Is one who is thrown into the Fire better, or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ This is an interrogative with the meaning of affirmation (taqrir), and its purpose is to alert that those who distort Our signs will be thrown into the Fire, while those who believe in Our signs will come secure on the Day of Resurrection. Then He said: ﴿Do as you wish; indeed He is Seeing of what you do﴾. This is also a third threat. Its parallel is what a formidable king says in severe anger when he begins to reproach some of his servants and then says to them: "Do as you wish," for this indicates a severe warning.

* * *

Then the Most High said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it comes to them﴾. This too is a threat, and concerning its response there are two views:

The first: its response is omitted, like all the omitted responses in the Qur'an, with the implied meaning: "Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it comes to them will be recompensed for their disbelief," or something similar.

The second: its response is His saying: ﴿They are called from a far place﴾ [Fussilat: 44]. The first is more correct.

[Page 114]

When He had gone to extremes in threatening those who distort the signs of the Qur'an, He followed it with an explanation of the Qur'an's greatness, saying: ﴿And indeed it is a Book of might (ʿazīz)﴾. The word ﴿عَزِيز﴾ (ʿazīz) has two meanings: the first is dominant and overpowering; the second is that whose like cannot be found. As for the Qur'an being ʿazīz in the sense of dominant, the matter is so, because by the strength of its proof it has overcome everything other than it. As for its being ʿazīz in the sense of incomparable, the matter is also so, because the earlier and later people have been unable to produce its equal. Then He said: ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it﴾. Concerning this there are several views:

The first: the earlier books, such as the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms, do not refute it, and no book will come after it that refutes it.

The second: what the Qur'an has ruled to be true does not become false, and what it has ruled to be false does not become true.

The third: its meaning is that it is protected from being diminished, so that falsehood would come to it from before it, or increased, so that falsehood would come to it from behind it. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is We who have sent down the Reminder, and indeed We will be its guardian﴾ [al-Hijr: 9]. The act of this falsehood is addition and subtraction.

The fourth: it may be that the intended meaning is that there will not be found in the future any book fit to be set up as its opponent, and there was not found in the past any book fit to be set up as its opponent.

The fifth: the author of al-Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari) said: this is an allegory (tamthil), and the intended meaning is that falsehood does not reach it, and finds no way to it from any direction whatsoever, so as to connect to it.

Know that Abu Muslim al-Isfahani may argue from this verse that naskh (abrogation) did not occur in it, because naskh is annulment (ibtal). If abrogation entered it, falsehood would have come to it from behind it, and that is contrary to this verse.

[p. 115]

Know that when He, may He be exalted, had threatened those who deny the signs of God, then explained the nobility of God's signs and the high rank of God's Book, He returned to the matter of the Messenger of God (ﷺ): that he should be patient with the harm of his people, and that his heart should not be constricted because of what He had related about them at the beginning of the surah, namely that they said, ﴿Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you invite us...﴾ up to His words, ﴿So work, indeed we are working﴾ [Fussilat: 5]. Then He said: ﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you﴾. On this there are two interpretations:

The first, which is the closer one: the meaning is that what the disbelievers of your people say to you is only like what the disbelievers of their peoples said to the messengers before them, of harmful words and slanders against the revealed Books. ﴿Indeed your Lord is Possessor of forgiveness﴾ for the truthful, ﴿and Possessor of painful punishment﴾ for the falsifiers. So entrust this matter to God and occupy yourself with what you have been commanded, which is conveying the message and calling to God, may He be exalted.

The second: the meaning is that God has said to you only what He said to all the other messengers, which is that He commanded you and commanded all the prophets to be patient with the foolishness of their peoples. Therefore it is incumbent upon Him that the people of His obedience hope in Him and that the people of His disobedience fear Him.

It has become clear from our discussion of the interpretation of this surah that its purpose is to answer their statement: ﴿They said, "Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you invite us, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a barrier, so work, indeed we are working"﴾. Sometimes He alerts to the corruption of this course, and sometimes He mentions promise and threat for whoever does not believe in this Qur'an and for whoever turns away from it. The discourse extended to this point from the beginning of the surah in good order and complete arrangement. Then He, may He be exalted, gave another answer to their statement, ﴿Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you invite us, and in our ears is deafness﴾. So He said: ﴿And if We had made it a non-Arabic Qur'an, they would have said, "Why have its verses not been explained in detail? Is it non-Arabic and [the messenger] Arab?"﴾. On this there are several issues:

The first issue: Hamzah, al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr, on the authority of 'Asim, read أأعجمي with two hamzas, as an interrogative (hamzat al-istifham, the interrogative hamza). The others read it with one hamza and a madd (lengthening), according to their usual practice in similar forms, such as ﴿أأنْذَرْتَهُمْ﴾ [al-Baqarah: 6] and similar ones, as interrogatives. It is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas with one hamza. As for reading with two hamzas: the first hamza is a hamza of denial, and the meaning is that they denied and said: the Qur'an is non-Arabic and the messenger is Arab, or the one addressed is Arab. As for reading without the interrogative hamza, the meaning is the statement that the Qur'an is non-Arabic and the one addressed is Arab.

The second issue: They related regarding the occasion of revelation of this verse that the disbelievers, out of obstinacy, said: "If the Qur'an had been revealed in the language of the non-Arabs," so this verse was revealed. In my view, expressions like these contain great injustice toward the Qur'an, because it requires the occurrence of verses that have no connection with one another, and it entails the greatest kind of slander. How then can the claim that it is an orderly Book be sustained, along with the commitment to such slander, let alone the claim that it is inimitable? Rather, the truth in my view is that this surah, from its beginning to its end, is one speech, according to what God related of their saying: ﴿Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you invite us, and in our ears is deafness﴾.

This statement is also connected to it and is an answer to it. The sense is: If We had revealed this Qur'an in the language of the non-Arabs, they would have had the right to say: "How did You send non-Arabic speech to an Arab people?" And it would be valid for them to say: ﴿Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you invite us﴾, that is, from this speech, ﴿and in our ears is deafness﴾ from it, because we do not understand it and do not grasp its meaning. But since We have revealed this Book in the language of the Arabs, and in their words, and you are of the people of this language, how can you claim that your hearts are in coverings from it, and that in your ears is deafness from it? It becomes clear that if we make this statement an answer to that statement, the surah from its beginning to its end remains in the best forms of arrangement. As for the way people mention it, it is very strange.

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Say: It is for those who believe a guidance and healing. And those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness, and it is blindness for them. Those are called from a distant place﴾.

Know that this is connected to their statement: ﴿They said, "Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you invite us"﴾ up to the end of the verse, as if He, may He be exalted, were saying:

[p. 116]

This speech I have sent to you in your own language, not in a foreign language unfamiliar to you, so you cannot say that our hearts are in coverings from it because of our ignorance of this language. It remains to be said that whoever God has given a nature inclined to the truth, a heart inclined to sincerity, and a resolve that calls him to exert effort in seeking the religion, this Qur'an will be for him a guidance and a healing.

As for its being a guidance: it is because it points to the good and guides to every felicity. As for its being "healing": when one is able to be guided, guidance has been attained, and that guidance is a healing for him from the sickness of disbelief and ignorance. As for one who is drowning in the sea of abandonment, wandering in the deserts of deprivation, and infatuated with following Satan, this Qur'an will be deafness in his ears, as He said: ﴿And in our ears is deafness﴾ [Fussilat: 5], and the Qur'an will be blindness for them, as He said: ﴿And between us and you is a barrier﴾ [Fussilat: 5]. ﴿Those are called from a distant place﴾, because of that barrier which stands between them and benefiting from the clarification of the Qur'an. Whoever is fair and does not force interpretation knows that when we interpret this verse in the way we have mentioned, this surah from its beginning to its end becomes one orderly speech, directed toward one aim.

Therefore this interpretation is better than what they mentioned. The majority read ﴿and it is blindness for them﴾ as a verbal noun (masdar). Ibn 'Abbas read عَمٍ as an adjective (na't). Abu 'Ubayd said: The first is the preferred reading, like His words ﴿guidance and healing﴾, and likewise ﴿blindness﴾, which is a verbal noun like them. If what was mentioned were that it is a guide and a healer, then the kasra in عَمٍ would be better, so that it would be an adjective like them. As for His words, may He be exalted, ﴿Those are called from a distant place﴾: Ibn 'Abbas said: He means like the beast that understands nothing but a call and a cry. It was also said: one who is called from a distant place does not hear, and if he hears he does not understand; so too is the condition of these people.

Likewise We have given you this Book; some of them have accepted it, and they are your companions, and others have rejected it, and they are the ones who say: ﴿Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you invite us﴾.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 41, verses 47–54 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour. No fruit comes out of its sheaths, nor does any female conceive or give birth except with His knowledge. On the day He calls to them, "Where are My partners?" they will say, "We declare to You that none of us bears witness."﴾ ﴿And what they used to invoke before has strayed from them, and they will think that they have no place of escape.﴾ ﴿Man does not tire of asking for good, but if evil touches him, he is despairing and hopeless.﴾ ﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after adversity has touched him, he will surely say, "This is mine, and I do not think the Hour will ever come. And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely have the best with Him." So We will inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and We will surely make them taste a severe punishment.﴾ ﴿And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself, and when evil touches him, he is one of lengthy supplication.﴾ ﴿Say, "Have you considered: if this is from Allah and you have disbelieved in it, who is more astray than one who is in extreme dissension?"﴾ ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. Is it not sufficient that your Lord is, over all things, a Witness?﴾ ﴿Unquestionably, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord. Unquestionably, He is all-encompassing of all things.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, threatened the disbelievers in the preceding verse with His saying, ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for himself, and whoever does evil, it is against it﴾, meaning that the recompense of each person reaches him on the Day of Resurrection, it is as if a questioner asked: "And when will that Day be?" So He, exalted is He, said that there is no way for creation to know that Day, and none knows it but Allah. Thus He said, ﴿To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour﴾. This phrase conveys restriction, i.e., none knows the precise time of the Hour except Allah. Just as this knowledge is with Allah alone, so too is the knowledge of the occurrence of future events at their specific times, which is with none but Allah, glorified and exalted. Then He mentioned two examples of this category: The first is His saying, ﴿nor does any fruit come out of its sheaths﴾, and the second is His saying, ﴿nor does any female conceive or give birth except with His knowledge﴾. Abu 'Ubayda said: "Akmamuhu" are its containers, which are that in which the fruit is, and its singular is kumm and kumma. with what began at the start of the surah. So He mentioned at the end of the surah the threat against those who ascribe partners and equals, saying: ﴿And the day He calls to them, "Where are My partners?"﴾, meaning according to your assumption and belief. * * *

Then He said: ﴿None of us bears witness﴾, and concerning this there are several interpretations:
First: None of us testifies that You have a partner; the meaning is that on that Day they disavow ascribing partners to Allah, exalted is He.
Second: None of us sees them, because they have strayed from them, and their gods have strayed from them, so they do not see them at the time of rebuke.
Third: That His saying ﴿None of us bears witness﴾ is the speech of the idols, for Allah gives them life, and then they say: None of us testifies to the truth of what they attributed to us of partnership. According to this interpretation, the meaning that they do not benefit them is as if they had strayed from them.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And they will think that they have no place of escape﴾. This is the beginning of a statement from Allah, exalted is He, saying: the disbelievers first thought, then became certain, that there is no escape for them from the Fire and the punishment. Some said: they first thought that there was no escape for them from the Fire, and then became certain of it afterward; but this is far-fetched, because the people of the Fire know that their punishment is eternal. When Allah, exalted is He, described the state of these disbelievers, that after persisting in asserting partners and rivals with Allah in this world, they disowned those partners in the Hereafter, He explained that man is in all times of changing conditions and varying course: if he perceives good and power, he swells up and becomes arrogant, and if he perceives affliction and trial, he wilts.

As it is said in the proverb: This is like the chameleon (qirrilā): if it sees good, it hangs down; if it sees evil, it turns away. So He said: ﴿Man does not tire of asking for good, but if evil touches him, he is despairing and hopeless﴾, an intensification in two respects:
One: through the pattern fa'ūl. Two: through repetition. Despair (al-yas) is a quality of the heart, while qunut is that apparent signs of despair show in the face and outward states.

Then Allah, exalted is He, explained that this one who has become hopeless and despairing, if blessing and fortune return to him, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after adversity has touched him﴾, this man comes with three kinds of corrupt statements and false doctrines that necessitate disbelief and distance from Allah, exalted is He:

The first of them is that he must say: "This is mine." In this there are two interpretations. First: its meaning is that this is my due which has reached me, because I have merited it by the virtues and deeds of righteousness and nearness to Allah that I have. The wretch does not know that no one has any claim against Allah for anything. For if that person is bare of virtues, this statement is manifestly corrupt; and if he is described by some virtues and praiseworthy qualities, they have all come to him only by the bounty and kindness of Allah. And when Allah bestows something upon one of His servants, that bestowal cannot become a cause for him to deserve something else from Allah. Thus the corruption of his saying "these good things came about because of my merit" is established by this. Second: "This is mine" means that it will not be removed from me and will remain for me and for my children and descendants.

The second of their corrupt utterances is that he says: ﴿And I do not think the Hour will ever come﴾, meaning that he has an intense desire for the world and great aversion to the Hereafter. When the matter concerns the affairs of this world, he says, "It is mine," and when the matter concerns the Hereafter, he says: ﴿And I do not think the Hour will ever come﴾.

The third of their corrupt utterances is that he says: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely have the best with Him﴾, meaning that the stronger in his assumption is that the claim of resurrection and the Last Day is false; and on the supposition that it is true, then surely he will have the best with Him. This statement indicates their certainty of reaching reward in several respects:
First: the particle "inna" conveys emphasis.
Second: placing "lī" first indicates this emphasis.
Third: His saying ﴿with Him﴾ indicates that those good things are present and prepared with Him, as one says: "I have with so-and-so such-and-such dinars," which conveys that they are present with him; whereas if you say, "I have such-and-such dinars owed to me by so-and-so," this does not convey that.
Fourth: the lam in ﴿la-l-ḥusnā﴾ conveys emphasis.
Fifth: ﴿la-l-ḥusnā﴾ conveys the perfection of the good.

When Allah, exalted is He, related these three corrupt statements of theirs, He said: ﴿So We will inform those who disbelieved of what they did﴾, meaning We will show them that the matter is the opposite of what they believed and the reverse of what they imagined, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan: 23]. ﴿And We will surely make them taste a severe punishment﴾ in return for their saying: ﴿Indeed, I have with Him the best.﴾

* * *

When Allah, exalted is He, related the statements of the one who was blessed after falling into calamities, He also related his actions, and said: ﴿And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away﴾ from reverence for the command of Allah and compassion toward the creatures of Allah, ﴿and distances himself﴾, meaning he goes off by himself, is arrogant and grows great. Then if harm and poverty touch him, he turns to persistent supplication and begins to plead and beseech. The word ʿarḍ (breadth) has been borrowed for the abundance and continuity of supplication; it is a attribute of bodies, and length is likewise borrowed by it, just as ghilaẓ (thickness) has been borrowed for the severity of punishment.

Know that when He, exalted is He, mentioned the great threat conditionally and explained that the polytheists would retract their claim of partnership on the Day of Resurrection, showing humiliation and submission because fear had overcome them, and explained that man is created to change: if he finds strength in himself he exceeds in arrogance and self-exaltation, and if he feels weakness and feebleness he exceeds in showing humility and need, He mentioned after this another statement that obliges these disbelievers not to exaggerate in showing aversion to accepting monotheism, and not to go to excess in showing enmity toward the Messenger ﷺ. He said: ﴿Say, "Have you considered: if this is from Allah and you have disbelieved in it, who is more astray than one who is in extreme dissension?"﴾ The sense of this statement is: whenever you hear this Qur'an, you turn away from it, do not reflect upon it, and exceed in aversion to it, until you say: ﴿Our hearts are in coverings against what you invite us to, and in our ears is deafness﴾.

Then it is known by necessity that knowledge that the Qur'an is false is not self-evident knowledge, and knowledge of the corruption of the doctrine of monotheism and prophethood is not self-evident knowledge. Before the proof, it is possible that it is correct and possible that it is corrupt. On the assumption that it is correct, your persistence in rejecting it is among the greatest causes of punishment. This approach obliges you to abandon this error and return to reflection and inference: if proof indicates its soundness, you accept it, and if it indicates its corruption, you abandon it. As for before the proof, persistence in rejection and turning away is far from reason. His saying ﴿who is in extreme dissension﴾ is placed in the position of "from among you," as an explanation of their state and attributes. When he had mentioned these many aspects in establishing monotheism and prophethood, and answered the doubts of the polytheists and the deceptions of the misguided, he said

صفحة ١٢٠

: ﴿We shall show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾. Al-Wahidi said: The singular of al-āfāq (horizons) is ufuq, which is a direction of the regions of the earth. Likewise, the horizons of the sky are its directions, its sides, and its edges. Regarding the interpretation of His words ﴿We shall show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves﴾, there are two opinions.

The first: the signs of the horizons refer to the celestial and stellar signs, the signs of night and day, the signs of light and of going astray, the darknesses, the signs of the world of the four elements, and the signs of the three kinds of generated beings (minerals, plants, and animals). God has mentioned many of these in the Qur'an. His words ﴿and within themselves﴾ refer to the proofs drawn from the manner in which embryos are formed in the darkness of the wombs, the emergence of the wondrous organs, and the strange compositions, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿And within yourselves; will you not see?﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 21]. The meaning is: We shall show them these proofs time after time until the doubts are removed from their hearts, and certainty and conviction of the existence of the God who is Powerful, Wise, and Knowing, free from any likeness or opposite, is attained in them.

If it is said: this view is weak, because His words ﴿We shall show them﴾ imply that God has not yet made them aware of those signs and will make them aware of them afterwards. But the signs present in the higher and lower worlds were already made known to them by God before that. Thus it is established that carrying this expression on this view is impossible. We reply: although the people had seen these things, the wonders that God has deposited in these things are without end. So He makes them aware of those wonders moment by moment. An example of this is that everyone has seen the structure of the human body with his own eyes and witnessed it, yet the wonders that God has originated in the composition of this body are numerous, and most people do not know them. Whoever has come to know some of them, the more he comes to know those wonders and marvels, the more the words ﴿We shall show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves﴾ are fulfilled in this way.

The second opinion: the signs of the horizons refer to the conquest of the lands surrounding Mecca, and the signs within themselves refer to the conquest of Mecca. Those who hold this opinion preferred it over the first, on the grounds that His words ﴿We shall show them﴾ suit this view and do not suit the first. However, we have answered this by saying that His words ﴿We shall show them﴾ suit the first view, as we have established.

If it is said: carrying the verse on this view is far-fetched, because at most the matter amounts to this: Muhammad (ﷺ) gained control over some of the lands surrounding Mecca, then gained control over Mecca. But gaining control over some lands does not indicate that the one who gains control is in the right. For we see that the unbelievers may gain control over the lands of Islam and over its rulers, and that does not indicate that they are in the right. For this reason we say that carrying the verse on the first view is preferable.

Then we say: if we wish to validate this view, we say: we do not argue merely from Muhammad's (ﷺ) gaining control over those lands to his being right in claiming prophethood. Rather, we argue from the fact that he (ﷺ) reported about Mecca that he would gain control over it, would subdue its people, and that his companions would become conquerors of the enemies. This is an announcement of the unseen, and its reported matter occurred in conformity with his report. Therefore this is a truthful announcement of the unseen, and the announcement of the unseen is a miracle. By this route, the attainment of this control is used as evidence that this religion is true.
* * *
Then He said: ﴿Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is witness over all things?﴾ The word ﴿your Lord﴾ is in the nominative position as the subject of ﴿suffices﴾, and ﴿that He is witness over all things﴾ is a substitute for it. Its underlying sense is: Is it not sufficient for them that your Lord is witness over all things? The meaning of God, exalted is He, being a witness over things is that He created the proofs for them. We have fully explained this in the interpretation of His words: ﴿Say: "What thing is greatest in testimony?" Say: "God"﴾ [al-An'am: 19]. The meaning is: Are these numerous proofs, which God, exalted is He, has made clear and established in this surah and in all the surahs of the Qur'an, not sufficient for them? They indicate the oneness of God, His transcendence, justice, and prophethood.

Then He concluded the surah with His words: ﴿Verily, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord﴾, meaning: the people are in great uncertainty and severe doubt concerning the resurrection and the Last Day. It has also been read as (fī muriyah) with a ḍammah.

Then He said: ﴿Verily, He encompasses all things﴾, meaning: He is knowing of all the knowables, which are without end. So He knows the inner and outer states of these unbelievers, and He recompenses each person for his deed according to what befits it: if good, then good; if evil, then evil. If it is said: His words ﴿Verily, He encompasses all things﴾ imply that His knowledge is finite. We reply: His words ﴿encompasses all things﴾ imply that His knowledge encompasses each one of the things. This implies that each one of them is finite, not that their totality is finite. And God knows best what is correct.
