When Allah, exalted is He, related these three corrupt statements of theirs, He said: ﴿So We will inform those who disbelieved of what they did﴾, meaning We will show them that the matter is the opposite of what they believed and the reverse of what they imagined, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan: 23]. ﴿And We will surely make them taste a severe punishment﴾ in return for their saying: ﴿Indeed, I have with Him the best.﴾

* * *

When Allah, exalted is He, related the statements of the one who was blessed after falling into calamities, He also related his actions, and said: ﴿And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away﴾ from reverence for the command of Allah and compassion toward the creatures of Allah, ﴿and distances himself﴾, meaning he goes off by himself, is arrogant and grows great. Then if harm and poverty touch him, he turns to persistent supplication and begins to plead and beseech. The word ʿarḍ (breadth) has been borrowed for the abundance and continuity of supplication; it is a attribute of bodies, and length is likewise borrowed by it, just as ghilaẓ (thickness) has been borrowed for the severity of punishment.

Know that when He, exalted is He, mentioned the great threat conditionally and explained that the polytheists would retract their claim of partnership on the Day of Resurrection, showing humiliation and submission because fear had overcome them, and explained that man is created to change: if he finds strength in himself he exceeds in arrogance and self-exaltation, and if he feels weakness and feebleness he exceeds in showing humility and need, He mentioned after this another statement that obliges these disbelievers not to exaggerate in showing aversion to accepting monotheism, and not to go to excess in showing enmity toward the Messenger ﷺ. He said: ﴿Say, "Have you considered: if this is from Allah and you have disbelieved in it, who is more astray than one who is in extreme dissension?"﴾ The sense of this statement is: whenever you hear this Qur'an, you turn away from it, do not reflect upon it, and exceed in aversion to it, until you say: ﴿Our hearts are in coverings against what you invite us to, and in our ears is deafness﴾.

Then it is known by necessity that knowledge that the Qur'an is false is not self-evident knowledge, and knowledge of the corruption of the doctrine of monotheism and prophethood is not self-evident knowledge. Before the proof, it is possible that it is correct and possible that it is corrupt. On the assumption that it is correct, your persistence in rejecting it is among the greatest causes of punishment. This approach obliges you to abandon this error and return to reflection and inference: if proof indicates its soundness, you accept it, and if it indicates its corruption, you abandon it. As for before the proof, persistence in rejection and turning away is far from reason. His saying ﴿who is in extreme dissension﴾ is placed in the position of "from among you," as an explanation of their state and attributes. When he had mentioned these many aspects in establishing monotheism and prophethood, and answered the doubts of the polytheists and the deceptions of the misguided, he said

: ﴿We shall show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾. Al-Wahidi said: The singular of al-āfāq (horizons) is ufuq, which is a direction of the regions of the earth. Likewise, the horizons of the sky are its directions, its sides, and its edges. Regarding the interpretation of His words ﴿We shall show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves﴾, there are two opinions.

The first: the signs of the horizons refer to the celestial and stellar signs, the signs of night and day, the signs of light and of going astray, the darknesses, the signs of the world of the four elements, and the signs of the three kinds of generated beings (minerals, plants, and animals). God has mentioned many of these in the Qur'an. His words ﴿and within themselves﴾ refer to the proofs drawn from the manner in which embryos are formed in the darkness of the wombs, the emergence of the wondrous organs, and the strange compositions, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿And within yourselves; will you not see?﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 21]. The meaning is: We shall show them these proofs time after time until the doubts are removed from their hearts, and certainty and conviction of the existence of the God who is Powerful, Wise, and Knowing, free from any likeness or opposite, is attained in them.

If it is said: this view is weak, because His words ﴿We shall show them﴾ imply that God has not yet made them aware of those signs and will make them aware of them afterwards. But the signs present in the higher and lower worlds were already made known to them by God before that. Thus it is established that carrying this expression on this view is impossible. We reply: although the people had seen these things, the wonders that God has deposited in these things are without end. So He makes them aware of those wonders moment by moment. An example of this is that everyone has seen the structure of the human body with his own eyes and witnessed it, yet the wonders that God has originated in the composition of this body are numerous, and most people do not know them. Whoever has come to know some of them, the more he comes to know those wonders and marvels, the more the words ﴿We shall show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves﴾ are fulfilled in this way.

The second opinion: the signs of the horizons refer to the conquest of the lands surrounding Mecca, and the signs within themselves refer to the conquest of Mecca. Those who hold this opinion preferred it over the first, on the grounds that His words ﴿We shall show them﴾ suit this view and do not suit the first. However, we have answered this by saying that His words ﴿We shall show them﴾ suit the first view, as we have established.

If it is said: carrying the verse on this view is far-fetched, because at most the matter amounts to this: Muhammad (ﷺ) gained control over some of the lands surrounding Mecca, then gained control over Mecca. But gaining control over some lands does not indicate that the one who gains control is in the right. For we see that the unbelievers may gain control over the lands of Islam and over its rulers, and that does not indicate that they are in the right. For this reason we say that carrying the verse on the first view is preferable.

Then we say: if we wish to validate this view, we say: we do not argue merely from Muhammad's (ﷺ) gaining control over those lands to his being right in claiming prophethood. Rather, we argue from the fact that he (ﷺ) reported about Mecca that he would gain control over it, would subdue its people, and that his companions would become conquerors of the enemies. This is an announcement of the unseen, and its reported matter occurred in conformity with his report. Therefore this is a truthful announcement of the unseen, and the announcement of the unseen is a miracle. By this route, the attainment of this control is used as evidence that this religion is true.
* * *
Then He said: ﴿Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is witness over all things?﴾ The word ﴿your Lord﴾ is in the nominative position as the subject of ﴿suffices﴾, and ﴿that He is witness over all things﴾ is a substitute for it. Its underlying sense is: Is it not sufficient for them that your Lord is witness over all things? Then He said: ﴿Verily, He encompasses all things﴾, meaning: He is knowing of all the knowables, which are without end. We say: the practitioners of these sciences cannot make any certain and definitive judgment about any matter whatsoever; the utmost they reach is the claim of a weak conjecture. What is mentioned in this verse is that its knowledge is with Allah alone, and knowledge is certainty and conviction. By this approach the contradiction is removed, and Allah knows best. Then, when He mentioned the Resurrection, He followed it with some of the conditions of the Day of Resurrection, and what He mentioned here is also closely connected

صفحة ١١٨

with what began at the start of the surah. That is because the beginning of the surah indicates that the intensity of their aversion to listening to the Qur'an arose from the fact that Muhammad ﷺ was calling them to monotheism and to disassociation from the idols and images, as is evidenced by his saying at the beginning of the surah: ﴿Say, "I am only a human being like you; it is revealed to me that your god is but one God."﴾ [Fussilat: 6]. So He mentioned at the end of the surah the threat against those who ascribe partners and equals, saying: ﴿And the day He calls to them, "Where are My partners?"﴾, meaning according to your assumption and belief. They will say, "We have informed You" (ādhannāka). Ibn 'Abbas said: "We have made You hear," as in His saying: ﴿and it hearkened to its Lord and was obligated﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 2], in the sense of "heard." Al-Kalbi said: "We have informed You." But this is far-fetched, because the people of the Resurrection know Allah and know that He knows things with a necessary knowledge, so informing Him is impossible.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿None of us bears witness﴾, and concerning this there are several interpretations:
First: None of us testifies that You have a partner; the meaning is that on that Day they disavow ascribing partners to Allah, exalted is He.
Second: None of us sees them, because they have strayed from them, and their gods have strayed from them, so they do not see them at the time of rebuke.
Third: That His saying ﴿None of us bears witness﴾ is the speech of the idols, for Allah gives them life, and then they say: None of us testifies to the truth of what they attributed to us of partnership. According to this interpretation, the meaning that they do not benefit them is as if they had strayed from them.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And they will think that they have no place of escape﴾. This is the beginning of a statement from Allah, exalted is He, saying: the disbelievers first thought, then became certain, that there is no escape for them from the Fire and the punishment. Some said: they first thought that there was no escape for them from the Fire, and then became certain of it afterward; but this is far-fetched, because the people of the Fire know that their punishment is eternal. When Allah, exalted is He, described the state of these disbelievers, that after persisting in asserting partners and rivals with Allah in this world, they disowned those partners in the Hereafter, He explained that man is in all times of changing conditions and varying course: if he perceives good and power, he swells up and becomes arrogant, and if he perceives affliction and trial, he wilts.

As it is said in the proverb: This is like the chameleon (qirrilā): if it sees good, it hangs down; if it sees evil, it turns away. So He said: ﴿Man does not tire of asking for good, but if evil touches him, he is despairing and hopeless﴾, an intensification in two respects:
One: through the pattern fa'ūl. Two: through repetition. Despair (al-yas) is a quality of the heart, while qunut is that apparent signs of despair show in the face and outward states.

Then Allah, exalted is He, explained that this one who has become hopeless and despairing, if blessing and fortune return to him, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after adversity has touched him﴾, this man comes with three kinds of corrupt statements and false doctrines that necessitate disbelief and distance from Allah, exalted is He:

The first of them is that he must say: "This is mine." In this there are two interpretations. First: its meaning is that this is my due which has reached me, because I have merited it by the virtues and deeds of righteousness and nearness to Allah that I have. The wretch does not know that no one has any claim against Allah for anything. For if that person is bare of virtues, this statement is manifestly corrupt; and if he is described by some virtues and praiseworthy qualities, they have all come to him only by the bounty and kindness of Allah. And when Allah bestows something upon one of His servants, that bestowal cannot become a cause for him to deserve something else from Allah. Thus the corruption of his saying "these good things came about because of my merit" is established by this. Second: "This is mine" means that it will not be removed from me and will remain for me and for my children and descendants.

The second of their corrupt utterances is that he says: ﴿And I do not think the Hour will ever come﴾, meaning that he has an intense desire for the world and great aversion to the Hereafter. When the matter concerns the affairs of this world, he says, "It is mine," and when the matter concerns the Hereafter, he says: ﴿And I do not think the Hour will ever come﴾.

The third of their corrupt utterances is that he says: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely have the best with Him﴾, meaning that the stronger in his assumption is that the claim of resurrection and the Last Day is false; and on the supposition that it is true, then surely he will have the best with Him. This statement indicates their certainty of reaching reward in several respects:
First: the particle "inna" conveys emphasis.
Second: placing "lī" first indicates this emphasis.
Third: His saying ﴿with Him﴾ indicates that those good things are present and prepared with Him, as one says: "I have with so-and-so such-and-such dinars," which conveys that they are present with him; whereas if you say, "I have such-and-such dinars owed to me by so-and-so," this does not convey that.
Fourth: the lam in ﴿la-l-ḥusnā﴾ conveys emphasis.
Fifth: ﴿la-l-ḥusnā﴾ conveys the perfection of the good.

When Allah, exalted is He, related these three corrupt statements of theirs, He said: ﴿So We will inform those who disbelieved of what they did﴾, meaning We will show them that the matter is the opposite of what they believed and the reverse of what they imagined, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan: 23]. ﴿And We will surely make them taste a severe punishment﴾ in return for their saying: ﴿Indeed, I have with Him the best.﴾

* * *

When Allah, exalted is He, related the statements of the one who was blessed after falling into calamities, He also related his actions, and said: ﴿And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away﴾ from reverence for the command of Allah and compassion toward the creatures of Allah, ﴿and distances himself﴾, meaning he goes off by himself, is arrogant and grows great. Then if harm and poverty touch him, he turns to persistent supplication and begins to plead and beseech. The word ʿarḍ (breadth) has been borrowed for the abundance and continuity of supplication; it is a attribute of bodies, and length is likewise borrowed by it, just as ghilaẓ (thickness) has been borrowed for the severity of punishment.

Know that when He, exalted is He, mentioned the great threat conditionally and explained that the polytheists would retract their claim of partnership on the Day of Resurrection, showing humiliation and submission because fear had overcome them, and explained that man is created to change: if he finds strength in himself he exceeds in arrogance and self-exaltation, and if he feels weakness and feebleness he exceeds in showing humility and need, He mentioned after this another statement that obliges these disbelievers not to exaggerate in showing aversion to accepting monotheism, and not to go to excess in showing enmity toward the Messenger ﷺ. He said: ﴿Say, "Have you considered: if this is from Allah and you have disbelieved in it, who is more astray than one who is in extreme dissension?"﴾ The sense of this statement is: whenever you hear this Qur'an, you turn away from it, do not reflect upon it, and exceed in aversion to it, until you say: ﴿Our hearts are in coverings against what you invite us to, and in our ears is deafness﴾.

Then it is known by necessity that knowledge that the Qur'an is false is not self-evident knowledge, and knowledge of the corruption of the doctrine of monotheism and prophethood is not self-evident knowledge. Before the proof, it is possible that it is correct and possible that it is corrupt. On the assumption that it is correct, your persistence in rejecting it is among the greatest causes of punishment. This approach obliges you to abandon this error and return to reflection and inference: if proof indicates its soundness, you accept it, and if it indicates its corruption, you abandon it. As for before the proof, persistence in rejection and turning away is far from reason. His saying ﴿who is in extreme dissension﴾ is placed in the position of "from among you," as an explanation of their state and attributes. When he had mentioned these many aspects in establishing monotheism and prophethood, and answered the doubts of the polytheists and the deceptions of the misguided, he said

صفحة ١٢٠

: ﴿We shall show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾. Al-Wahidi said: The singular of al-āfāq (horizons) is ufuq, which is a direction of the regions of the earth. Likewise, the horizons of the sky are its directions, its sides, and its edges. Regarding the interpretation of His words ﴿We shall show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves﴾, there are two opinions.

The first: the signs of the horizons refer to the celestial and stellar signs, the signs of night and day, the signs of light and of going astray, the darknesses, the signs of the world of the four elements, and the signs of the three kinds of generated beings (minerals, plants, and animals). God has mentioned many of these in the Qur'an. His words ﴿and within themselves﴾ refer to the proofs drawn from the manner in which embryos are formed in the darkness of the wombs, the emergence of the wondrous organs, and the strange compositions, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿And within yourselves; will you not see?﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 21]. The meaning is: We shall show them these proofs time after time until the doubts are removed from their hearts, and certainty and conviction of the existence of the God who is Powerful, Wise, and Knowing, free from any likeness or opposite, is attained in them.

If it is said: this view is weak, because His words ﴿We shall show them﴾ imply that God has not yet made them aware of those signs and will make them aware of them afterwards. But the signs present in the higher and lower worlds were already made known to them by God before that. Thus it is established that carrying this expression on this view is impossible. We reply: although the people had seen these things, the wonders that God has deposited in these things are without end. So He makes them aware of those wonders moment by moment. An example of this is that everyone has seen the structure of the human body with his own eyes and witnessed it, yet the wonders that God has originated in the composition of this body are numerous, and most people do not know them. Whoever has come to know some of them, the more he comes to know those wonders and marvels, the more the words ﴿We shall show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves﴾ are fulfilled in this way.

The second opinion: the signs of the horizons refer to the conquest of the lands surrounding Mecca, and the signs within themselves refer to the conquest of Mecca. Those who hold this opinion preferred it over the first, on the grounds that His words ﴿We shall show them﴾ suit this view and do not suit the first. However, we have answered this by saying that His words ﴿We shall show them﴾ suit the first view, as we have established.

If it is said: carrying the verse on this view is far-fetched, because at most the matter amounts to this: Muhammad (ﷺ) gained control over some of the lands surrounding Mecca, then gained control over Mecca. But gaining control over some lands does not indicate that the one who gains control is in the right. For we see that the unbelievers may gain control over the lands of Islam and over its rulers, and that does not indicate that they are in the right. For this reason we say that carrying the verse on the first view is preferable.

Then we say: if we wish to validate this view, we say: we do not argue merely from Muhammad's (ﷺ) gaining control over those lands to his being right in claiming prophethood. Rather, we argue from the fact that he (ﷺ) reported about Mecca that he would gain control over it, would subdue its people, and that his companions would become conquerors of the enemies. This is an announcement of the unseen, and its reported matter occurred in conformity with his report. Therefore this is a truthful announcement of the unseen, and the announcement of the unseen is a miracle. By this route, the attainment of this control is used as evidence that this religion is true.
* * *
Then He said: ﴿Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is witness over all things?﴾ The word ﴿your Lord﴾ is in the nominative position as the subject of ﴿suffices﴾, and ﴿that He is witness over all things﴾ is a substitute for it. Its underlying sense is: Is it not sufficient for them that your Lord is witness over all things? The meaning of God, exalted is He, being a witness over things is that He created the proofs for them. We have fully explained this in the interpretation of His words: ﴿Say: "What thing is greatest in testimony?" Say: "God"﴾ [al-An'am: 19]. The meaning is: Are these numerous proofs, which God, exalted is He, has made clear and established in this surah and in all the surahs of the Qur'an, not sufficient for them? They indicate the oneness of God, His transcendence, justice, and prophethood.

Then He concluded the surah with His words: ﴿Verily, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord﴾, meaning: the people are in great uncertainty and severe doubt concerning the resurrection and the Last Day. It has also been read as (fī muriyah) with a ḍammah.

Then He said: ﴿Verily, He encompasses all things﴾, meaning: He is knowing of all the knowables, which are without end. So He knows the inner and outer states of these unbelievers, and He recompenses each person for his deed according to what befits it: if good, then good; if evil, then evil. If it is said: His words ﴿Verily, He encompasses all things﴾ imply that His knowledge is finite. We reply: His words ﴿encompasses all things﴾ imply that His knowledge encompasses each one of the things. This implies that each one of them is finite, not that their totality is finite. And God knows best what is correct.

Rather, we argue from the fact that he (ﷺ) reported about Mecca that he would gain control over it, would subdue its people, and that his companions would become conquerors of the enemies. This is an announcement of the unseen, and its reported matter occurred in conformity with his report. Therefore this is a truthful announcement of the unseen, and the announcement of the unseen is a miracle. By this route, the attainment of this control is used as evidence that this religion is true.
* * *
Then He said: ﴿Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is witness over all things?﴾ The word ﴿your Lord﴾ is in the nominative position as the subject of ﴿suffices﴾, and ﴿that He is witness over all things﴾ is a substitute for it. Its underlying sense is: Is it not sufficient for them that your Lord is witness over all things? The meaning of God, exalted is He, being a witness over things is that He created the proofs for them. We have fully explained this in the interpretation of His words: ﴿Say: "What thing is greatest in testimony?" Say: "God"﴾ [al-An'am: 19]. The meaning is: Are these numerous proofs, which God, exalted is He, has made clear and established in this surah and in all the surahs of the Qur'an, not sufficient for them? They indicate the oneness of God, His transcendence, justice, and prophethood.

Then He concluded the surah with His words: ﴿Verily, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord﴾, meaning: the people are in great uncertainty and severe doubt concerning the resurrection and the Last Day. It has also been read as (fī muriyah) with a ḍammah.

Page 121

Then He said: ﴿Verily, He encompasses all things﴾, meaning: He is knowing of all the knowables, which are without end. So He knows the inner and outer states of these unbelievers, and He recompenses each person for his deed according to what befits it: if good, then good; if evil, then evil. If it is said: His words ﴿Verily, He encompasses all things﴾ imply that His knowledge is finite. We reply: His words ﴿encompasses all things﴾ imply that His knowledge encompasses each one of the things. This implies that each one of them is finite, not that their totality is finite. And God knows best what is correct.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 41, verses 47–54 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour. No fruit comes out of its sheaths, nor does any female conceive or give birth except with His knowledge. On the day He calls to them, "Where are My partners?" they will say, "We declare to You that none of us bears witness."﴾ ﴿And what they used to invoke before has strayed from them, and they will think that they have no place of escape.﴾ ﴿Man does not tire of asking for good, but if evil touches him, he is despairing and hopeless.﴾ ﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after adversity has touched him, he will surely say, "This is mine, and I do not think the Hour will ever come. And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely have the best with Him." So We will inform those who disbelieved of what they did, and We will surely make them taste a severe punishment.﴾ ﴿And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself, and when evil touches him, he is one of lengthy supplication.﴾ ﴿Say, "Have you considered: if this is from Allah and you have disbelieved in it, who is more astray than one who is in extreme dissension?"﴾ ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. Is it not sufficient that your Lord is, over all things, a Witness?﴾ ﴿Unquestionably, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord. Unquestionably, He is all-encompassing of all things.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, threatened the disbelievers in the preceding verse with His saying, ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for himself, and whoever does evil, it is against it﴾, meaning that the recompense of each person reaches him on the Day of Resurrection, it is as if a questioner asked: "And when will that Day be?" So He, exalted is He, said that there is no way for creation to know that Day, and none knows it but Allah. Thus He said, ﴿To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour﴾. This phrase conveys restriction, i.e., none knows the precise time of the Hour except Allah. Just as this knowledge is with Allah alone, so too is the knowledge of the occurrence of future events at their specific times, which is with none but Allah, glorified and exalted. Then He mentioned two examples of this category: The first is His saying, ﴿nor does any fruit come out of its sheaths﴾, and the second is His saying, ﴿nor does any female conceive or give birth except with His knowledge﴾. Abu 'Ubayda said: "Akmamuhu" are its containers, which are that in which the fruit is, and its singular is kumm and kumma. Nafi', Ibn 'Amir and Hafs from 'Asim read ﴿min thamarat﴾ with an alif, in the plural, while the rest read ﴿min thamarah﴾ without an alif, in the singular.

Know that a parallel to this verse is His saying: ﴿Indeed, with Allah is the knowledge of the Hour, and He sends down the rain﴾ up to the end of the verse. If it is said: Do not astrologers, from the rising of the year's ascendant, come to know many conditions of the world, and likewise from the ascendants of people they come to know things of their circumstances, and there is another thing here called the science of geomancy (ilm al-raml), which is often accurate? Also, the science of dream interpretation (ta'bir), by general agreement, may indicate the states of unseen matters. How then is it to be reconciled between these observed sciences and this verse? We say: the practitioners of these sciences cannot make any certain and definitive judgment about any matter whatsoever; the utmost they reach is the claim of a weak conjecture. What is mentioned in this verse is that its knowledge is with Allah alone, and knowledge is certainty and conviction. By this approach the contradiction is removed, and Allah knows best. Then, when He mentioned the Resurrection, He followed it with some of the conditions of the Day of Resurrection, and what He mentioned here is also closely connected

صفحة ١١٨

with what began at the start of the surah. That is because the beginning of the surah indicates that the intensity of their aversion to listening to the Qur'an arose from the fact that Muhammad ﷺ was calling them to monotheism and to disassociation from the idols and images, as is evidenced by his saying at the beginning of the surah: ﴿Say, "I am only a human being like you; it is revealed to me that your god is but one God."﴾ [Fussilat: 6]. So He mentioned at the end of the surah the threat against those who ascribe partners and equals, saying: ﴿And the day He calls to them, "Where are My partners?"﴾, meaning according to your assumption and belief. They will say, "We have informed You" (ādhannāka). Ibn 'Abbas said: "We have made You hear," as in His saying: ﴿and it hearkened to its Lord and was obligated﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 2], in the sense of "heard." Al-Kalbi said: "We have informed You." But this is far-fetched, because the people of the Resurrection know Allah and know that He knows things with a necessary knowledge, so informing Him is impossible.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿None of us bears witness﴾, and concerning this there are several interpretations:
First: None of us testifies that You have a partner; the meaning is that on that Day they disavow ascribing partners to Allah, exalted is He.
Second: None of us sees them, because they have strayed from them, and their gods have strayed from them, so they do not see them at the time of rebuke.
Third: That His saying ﴿None of us bears witness﴾ is the speech of the idols, for Allah gives them life, and then they say: None of us testifies to the truth of what they attributed to us of partnership. According to this interpretation, the meaning that they do not benefit them is as if they had strayed from them.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And they will think that they have no place of escape﴾. This is the beginning of a statement from Allah, exalted is He, saying: the disbelievers first thought, then became certain, that there is no escape for them from the Fire and the punishment. Some said: they first thought that there was no escape for them from the Fire, and then became certain of it afterward; but this is far-fetched, because the people of the Fire know that their punishment is eternal. When Allah, exalted is He, described the state of these disbelievers, that after persisting in asserting partners and rivals with Allah in this world, they disowned those partners in the Hereafter, He explained that man is in all times of changing conditions and varying course: if he perceives good and power, he swells up and becomes arrogant, and if he perceives affliction and trial, he wilts.

As it is said in the proverb: This is like the chameleon (qirrilā): if it sees good, it hangs down; if it sees evil, it turns away. So He said: ﴿Man does not tire of asking for good, but if evil touches him, he is despairing and hopeless﴾, an intensification in two respects:
One: through the pattern fa'ūl. Two: through repetition. Despair (al-yas) is a quality of the heart, while qunut is that apparent signs of despair show in the face and outward states.

Then Allah, exalted is He, explained that this one who has become hopeless and despairing, if blessing and fortune return to him, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿And if We let him taste mercy from Us after adversity has touched him﴾, this man comes with three kinds of corrupt statements and false doctrines that necessitate disbelief and distance from Allah, exalted is He:

The first of them is that he must say: "This is mine." In this there are two interpretations. First: its meaning is that this is my due which has reached me, because I have merited it by the virtues and deeds of righteousness and nearness to Allah that I have. The wretch does not know that no one has any claim against Allah for anything. For if that person is bare of virtues, this statement is manifestly corrupt; and if he is described by some virtues and praiseworthy qualities, they have all come to him only by the bounty and kindness of Allah. And when Allah bestows something upon one of His servants, that bestowal cannot become a cause for him to deserve something else from Allah. Thus the corruption of his saying "these good things came about because of my merit" is established by this. Second: "This is mine" means that it will not be removed from me and will remain for me and for my children and descendants.

The second of their corrupt utterances is that he says: ﴿And I do not think the Hour will ever come﴾, meaning that he has an intense desire for the world and great aversion to the Hereafter. When the matter concerns the affairs of this world, he says, "It is mine," and when the matter concerns the Hereafter, he says: ﴿And I do not think the Hour will ever come﴾.

The third of their corrupt utterances is that he says: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord, I will surely have the best with Him﴾, meaning that the stronger in his assumption is that the claim of resurrection and the Last Day is false; and on the supposition that it is true, then surely he will have the best with Him. This statement indicates their certainty of reaching reward in several respects:
First: the particle "inna" conveys emphasis.
Second: placing "lī" first indicates this emphasis.
Third: His saying ﴿with Him﴾ indicates that those good things are present and prepared with Him, as one says: "I have with so-and-so such-and-such dinars," which conveys that they are present with him; whereas if you say, "I have such-and-such dinars owed to me by so-and-so," this does not convey that.
Fourth: the lam in ﴿la-l-ḥusnā﴾ conveys emphasis.
Fifth: ﴿la-l-ḥusnā﴾ conveys the perfection of the good.

When Allah, exalted is He, related these three corrupt statements of theirs, He said: ﴿So We will inform those who disbelieved of what they did﴾, meaning We will show them that the matter is the opposite of what they believed and the reverse of what they imagined, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan: 23]. ﴿And We will surely make them taste a severe punishment﴾ in return for their saying: ﴿Indeed, I have with Him the best.﴾

* * *

When Allah, exalted is He, related the statements of the one who was blessed after falling into calamities, He also related his actions, and said: ﴿And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away﴾ from reverence for the command of Allah and compassion toward the creatures of Allah, ﴿and distances himself﴾, meaning he goes off by himself, is arrogant and grows great. Then if harm and poverty touch him, he turns to persistent supplication and begins to plead and beseech. The word ʿarḍ (breadth) has been borrowed for the abundance and continuity of supplication; it is a attribute of bodies, and length is likewise borrowed by it, just as ghilaẓ (thickness) has been borrowed for the severity of punishment.

Know that when He, exalted is He, mentioned the great threat conditionally and explained that the polytheists would retract their claim of partnership on the Day of Resurrection, showing humiliation and submission because fear had overcome them, and explained that man is created to change: if he finds strength in himself he exceeds in arrogance and self-exaltation, and if he feels weakness and feebleness he exceeds in showing humility and need, He mentioned after this another statement that obliges these disbelievers not to exaggerate in showing aversion to accepting monotheism, and not to go to excess in showing enmity toward the Messenger ﷺ. He said: ﴿Say, "Have you considered: if this is from Allah and you have disbelieved in it, who is more astray than one who is in extreme dissension?"﴾ The sense of this statement is: whenever you hear this Qur'an, you turn away from it, do not reflect upon it, and exceed in aversion to it, until you say: ﴿Our hearts are in coverings against what you invite us to, and in our ears is deafness﴾.

Then it is known by necessity that knowledge that the Qur'an is false is not self-evident knowledge, and knowledge of the corruption of the doctrine of monotheism and prophethood is not self-evident knowledge. Before the proof, it is possible that it is correct and possible that it is corrupt. On the assumption that it is correct, your persistence in rejecting it is among the greatest causes of punishment. This approach obliges you to abandon this error and return to reflection and inference: if proof indicates its soundness, you accept it, and if it indicates its corruption, you abandon it. As for before the proof, persistence in rejection and turning away is far from reason. His saying ﴿who is in extreme dissension﴾ is placed in the position of "from among you," as an explanation of their state and attributes. When he had mentioned these many aspects in establishing monotheism and prophethood, and answered the doubts of the polytheists and the deceptions of the misguided, he said

صفحة ١٢٠

: ﴿We shall show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves, until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾. Al-Wahidi said: The singular of al-āfāq (horizons) is ufuq, which is a direction of the regions of the earth. Likewise, the horizons of the sky are its directions, its sides, and its edges. Regarding the interpretation of His words ﴿We shall show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves﴾, there are two opinions.

The first: the signs of the horizons refer to the celestial and stellar signs, the signs of night and day, the signs of light and of going astray, the darknesses, the signs of the world of the four elements, and the signs of the three kinds of generated beings (minerals, plants, and animals). God has mentioned many of these in the Qur'an. His words ﴿and within themselves﴾ refer to the proofs drawn from the manner in which embryos are formed in the darkness of the wombs, the emergence of the wondrous organs, and the strange compositions, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿And within yourselves; will you not see?﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 21]. The meaning is: We shall show them these proofs time after time until the doubts are removed from their hearts, and certainty and conviction of the existence of the God who is Powerful, Wise, and Knowing, free from any likeness or opposite, is attained in them.

If it is said: this view is weak, because His words ﴿We shall show them﴾ imply that God has not yet made them aware of those signs and will make them aware of them afterwards. But the signs present in the higher and lower worlds were already made known to them by God before that. Thus it is established that carrying this expression on this view is impossible. We reply: although the people had seen these things, the wonders that God has deposited in these things are without end. So He makes them aware of those wonders moment by moment. An example of this is that everyone has seen the structure of the human body with his own eyes and witnessed it, yet the wonders that God has originated in the composition of this body are numerous, and most people do not know them. Whoever has come to know some of them, the more he comes to know those wonders and marvels, the more the words ﴿We shall show them Our signs on the horizons and within themselves﴾ are fulfilled in this way.

The second opinion: the signs of the horizons refer to the conquest of the lands surrounding Mecca, and the signs within themselves refer to the conquest of Mecca. Those who hold this opinion preferred it over the first, on the grounds that His words ﴿We shall show them﴾ suit this view and do not suit the first. However, we have answered this by saying that His words ﴿We shall show them﴾ suit the first view, as we have established.

If it is said: carrying the verse on this view is far-fetched, because at most the matter amounts to this: Muhammad (ﷺ) gained control over some of the lands surrounding Mecca, then gained control over Mecca. But gaining control over some lands does not indicate that the one who gains control is in the right. For we see that the unbelievers may gain control over the lands of Islam and over its rulers, and that does not indicate that they are in the right. For this reason we say that carrying the verse on the first view is preferable.

Then we say: if we wish to validate this view, we say: we do not argue merely from Muhammad's (ﷺ) gaining control over those lands to his being right in claiming prophethood. Rather, we argue from the fact that he (ﷺ) reported about Mecca that he would gain control over it, would subdue its people, and that his companions would become conquerors of the enemies. This is an announcement of the unseen, and its reported matter occurred in conformity with his report. Therefore this is a truthful announcement of the unseen, and the announcement of the unseen is a miracle. By this route, the attainment of this control is used as evidence that this religion is true.
